title: Rainbow stripes, a backward R and a giraffe
label: Brand gallery
lede: The brand was built to be read from a moving car: letters in six colours, a striped facade and a mascot tall enough to see over the shelves. Here it is as it survives in photographs and the archive, with our drawings in the same spirit.

archive.caption: The logo with a star behind the R, as it appeared on the home page in December 2003.
archive.alt: Toys R Us logo in multicoloured letters with a star behind the R
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of toysrus.com.[^38] Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: A store in Boardman, Ohio, that kept its older facade to the end: striped panels, a brown mansard roof and the earlier lettering. Photographed on its last day, June 27, 2018, according to the photographer.
archive.alt: Older style Toys R Us storefront with rainbow striped panels and a brown roof
archive.credit: Photo: Larry Hachucka, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:VINTAGE_Toys_%E2%80%9CR%E2%80%9D_Us;_Boardman_Ohio.jpg), CC BY-SA 4.0.

archive.caption: The later blue-box storefront in Modesto, California, with its going-out-of-business banner.
archive.alt: Blue Toys R Us store with a going out of business banner

archive.caption: A later Times Square store, two days before it closed, according to the photographer. The original flagship there had closed in December 2015.[^36]
archive.alt: Shoppers inside a Toys R Us store with everything must go signs

archive.caption: The liquidation sale in Muncie, Indiana, twelve days before the end.
archive.alt: Empty shelves and caution tape in a closing store
archive.credit: Photo: Talor Berthelson, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Toys_%22R%22_Us_Store_Closing_01.jpg), CC BY 2.0.
